flagship.title: A two-mile turn over Mayo Mountain
flagship.standfirst: A modest hardwood loop from the picnic shelter, with a shorter inner loop if Rupert has had enough.
flagship.why_this_week: Start at the main Mayo Mountain access and take the blue two-mile loop through mixed hardwoods. The park describes a creek and seasonal views of Cedar Mountain; neither calls for leaving the trail. Keep the red half-mile inner loop in reserve for a shorter walk, and leave the separate waterfall and river accesses for another day. Finish in daylight and heed the earlier access closing time. The dated forecast puts both days in the low 50s after cold nights. A late-morning start gives the shaded path some time to warm; wet leaves can still hide slick roots.

panels.label: Start at the picnic shelter
panels.text: The blue Mayo Mountain Loop is two miles. Use the main access and designated picnic shelter parking, not a river launch or waterfall lot.

panels.label: Keep the red loop in reserve
panels.text: The red inner loop is half a mile. Keep Rupert leashed and turn back if wet leaves hide unsafe footing.

artwork.brief: Restrained environmental print after inspecting Plates 009–014 plus 006. Recent work is mixed: flat oxblood frontal walk, autumn woodland frontal seat, waterside recline, navy play bow, standing meadow and seated olive rear turn. This plate uses a nose-low side-on walking silhouette across a diagonal bank, pale trunks at the far right and a large slate-blue upper field; more depth than the last olive portrait, less detail than the layered woodland. Fine cream lines, one mustard collar, long Labrador muzzle and slim tapered tail. Independent of destination.

pivot.if: Thunder, high water, unsafe footing, strong wind or official closure
pivot.note: Postpone and recheck official park status and NWS. Do not substitute another exposed outing.

conditions.trail_note: Watch for frost on shaded ground and slick leaves over roots. Stay clear of creek banks; turn back if footing is unsafe. The red inner loop is a distance option only when its footing is sound.

practical.best_window: Start in late morning after checking park status and the latest forecast. Allow up to two hours and finish well before dusk and the earlier 5 p.m. closing time.
practical.fees: Free ordinary day use; reservations are separate.
practical.closures_note: Current official home, access page, trail page, news and map reviewed. No posted closure for Mayo Mountain access found. Main access GPS 36.4391,-79.9475, 500 Old Mayo Park Road. Start at picnic shelter parking. Blue two-mile easy loop with red half-mile inner loop. Free ordinary day use, use earlier 5 p.m. access close despite general 6 p.m. park close. Attended leash up to six feet; no pets inside buildings. Stay on trail; other river accesses are outside this itinerary.
